items.title: Jimmy Wormworth interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: another guy who I met around the same time who was a Hamilton College student had taken a band himself, his name was George Rutter... That’s how I knew George Rutter lived in St. Louis. And so on the way out to California one time I had a layover in St. Louis and called him from the airport.

ctx.x: Before I forget I need to ask you about this Hamilton College connection that I just learned about tonight with you.

Well in I guess the spring of 1956 Ronnie Zito may have contacted me to ask me if I wanted to go to Europe with these college guys who played Dixieland. And a couple of them went to Hamilton College and so forth. I don’t think I knew them. Either that or he recommended me to them. And to make a long story short I went with them. Ronnie’s mother wouldn’t let him go. So I went. And I became fast friends with almost all of them. A couple were Hamilton College students, I think one, the clarinet player, was a…

mostly stayed in Hague. We worked for about a month in the Hague, well in the resort Skathington outside the Hague, and then we just did sightseeing the rest of the time. And another guy who I met around the same time who was a Hamilton College student had taken a band himself, his name was George Rutter. I can’t remember what he played. Piano. He lives in St. Louis now. I was on the way to California and I don’t remember — oh I know, Lou Donaldson was in St. Louis and George Rutter went, this is fifteen years or…
